clue.text: Row as spaceship advanced for oxygen

indicators.note: 'advanced for oxygen' asks for one letter to stand in place of another inside the spaceship word

parts.note: a rocket is a spacecraft
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
A is a standard abbreviation for advanced, as in A level

explanation.surface: An argument breaks out over a spacecraft being sent up with something swapped for its oxygen supply.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is a noisy din or commotion, and a row in British speech is a loud disturbance or quarrel.

clue.text: Instructions: put boiled rice on edges of plate

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the first piece above the second
boiled rice is stirred and churned, signalling the letters of rice are rearranged
edges of takes the first and last letters of plate

explanation.surface: Cooking directions: serve boiled rice around the rim of the plate.
explanation.definitionFit: A recipe is a set of cooking directions for making a dish.

clue.text: A leader in Turkey supporting deception over line in pact

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the deception word above the line word
supporting means sitting beneath, so these letters come lower down

parts.note: a con is a swindle or deception
a cord is a line or string

indicators.note: leader in picks the first letter of Turkey

explanation.surface: A Turkish leader is backing a deceptive treaty clause.
explanation.definitionFit: A concordat is a formal agreement, especially between the Vatican and a state.

clue.text: Put out mischievous text about elected Conservative

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters are placed around the next pieces
mischievous text has been played with, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: in means elected, as a party that gets in

explanation.surface: A naughty message about a Tory MP's election is published.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mischievous' gives the jumble EXTT; 'about' then wraps it round the two short pieces. In British politics 'in' is what an elected party is.
explanation.definitionFit: Extinct means extinguished, as a fire or volcano that has been put out.

clue.text: Page in small book shows butter knife, for example

indicators.note: 'Page in' tells us the page letter is set inside the words that follow

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a reader is a book used for learning to read

explanation.surface: A page in a little book illustrates a kitchen utensil.
explanation.definitionFit: A butter knife is an instance of a tool for spreading, a blunt blade for smearing butter on bread.

clue.text: Leading player waving to organist after start of pastorale

indicators.note: after places the jumbled letters behind the picked letter
start of takes the first letter of pastorale
waving suggests movement back and forth, so to and organist are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lead performer gestures to the organ player once the pastoral piece begins.
explanation.definitionFit: The protagonist is the main character or chief participant in a drama or contest.

clue.text: Choose artist to portray complex Greek girl

parts.note: to elect is to choose
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Pick a painter to depict a troubled Greek young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' is the clever touch: the Electra complex, a daughter's fixation on her father, is named after her.
explanation.definitionFit: Electra is the daughter of Agamemnon in Greek myth, who gives her name to a psychological complex.

clue.text: Funny turn after onset of dizziness

indicators.note: after places the turn word behind the picked letter
onset of takes the first letter of dizziness

parts.note: a roll is a turn, as of an aircraft

explanation.surface: A comic spin follows the first sign of feeling giddy.
explanation.definitionFit: Droll means amusing in a dry or odd way.

clue.text: Broadcasting about egg production?

parts.note: re means about or concerning
laying is how hens produce eggs

explanation.surface: A transmission covering how hens produce eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Relaying a programme is passing on or transmitting it, as broadcasting does.

clue.text: Shrewd to include an early king of England

indicators.note: the shrewd word is made to include the next piece, holding it inside itself

parts.note: cute can mean clever or shrewd, as in a cute move

explanation.surface: A shrewd early English monarch is being described.
explanation.definitionFit: Canute (Cnut) was a Danish king who ruled England in the eleventh century.

clue.text: Sprang up to deliver receptacle for flowers, as trophy?

parts.note: rose is the past tense of rise, to spring up
to bowl is to deliver the ball in cricket

explanation.surface: Someone leapt up to hand over a vase that might double as a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the trophy sense: Rose Bowls are prize cups, and an American football stadium shares the name.
explanation.definitionFit: A rose bowl is a shallow dish for displaying cut flowers, often given as a sporting prize.

clue.text: Chap, one I transported across island in ancient land

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are spread across the island letter, which ends up within them
transported means carried off and rearranged, signalling an anagram of chap, one and I

explanation.surface: A man and I were carried over to an island in an old country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transported' scrambles CHAPONEI, and 'across' places the I for island within that scramble.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoenicia was an ancient seafaring civilisation on the eastern Mediterranean coast, in modern Lebanon.

clue.text: Ingratiate oneself to groom with act of kindness

parts.note: to curry a horse is to groom it with a currycomb
a favour is an act of kindness

explanation.surface: A stable hand grooms a horse as a kind gesture to win approval.
explanation.definitionFit: To curry favour is the idiom for seeking someone's goodwill by flattery.

clue.text: Correspond with supporter after end of test

indicators.note: the supporter word is placed after the picked letter
end of picks the final letter of the word test

parts.note: an ally is someone who supports you

explanation.surface: A test result matches what a backer expected.
explanation.definitionFit: To tally is to agree or match up, as when two accounts tally.

clue.text: Put off speech about one in decline

indicators.note: about means the two words together go around the piece for one

parts.note: to deter is to discourage or put off
an oration is a formal speech
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone postpones a talk about a person in decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the two-word combination round the numeral, so it lands at the join between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Deterioration is a worsening or falling off in condition, which is what a decline is.

clue.text: Up for a swing instrumental?

definitions.meaning: being up for something means keen or willing to do it
a famous Glenn Miller big-band swing number with no vocals

explanation.surface: Someone asks if you fancy a dance to some swing music.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means feeling inclined to do something, and is also the title of Glenn Miller's 1939 swing hit.

clue.text: Rating on manoeuvres in the dark

indicators.note: a sailor on manoeuvres moves about, signalling rating and on are rearranged

explanation.surface: A naval rating on exercises is operating at night.
explanation.walkthrough: A rating is a non-officer sailor in the Royal Navy; 'on manoeuvres' looks like one phrase, but 'on' is part of the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the dark about something means not knowing, lacking information.

clue.text: Learn about what is going on round a track and avoid being caught

indicators.note: round means the first phrase is wrapped round the piece made from a and track

parts.words: Learn about what is going on
parts.note: to get with it is slang for becoming up to date and aware
a way is a path or track

explanation.surface: Someone finds out about events around a racetrack and slips away unnoticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' splits the slang phrase after its first word so the track piece sits within it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to do something wrong and escape detection or punishment.

clue.text: Swears violently catching second fish

indicators.note: catching means the jumbled letters close round the next piece
violently means the letters of swears are thrown about

explanation.surface: An angler curses furiously on landing another fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrasses are a family of brightly coloured marine fish.

clue.text: Male circle welcoming a trial

indicators.note: welcoming means taking a guest in, so the a sits inside

parts.note: he refers to a male
a ring is a circle

explanation.surface: A circle of men welcomes a newcomer on probation.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearing is a trial or judicial examination of a case.

clue.text: Queen of Persia protected by Xerxes there

indicators.note: protected by says the letters sit safely inside the words Xerxes there

explanation.surface: A Persian queen is kept safe by her king Xerxes.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible, Esther became queen to the Persian king Ahasuerus, often identified with Xerxes.

clue.text: Some from a hallowed place in Nebraska

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something taken from a sacred spot in the American Midwest.
explanation.definitionFit: Omaha is the largest city in the US state of Nebraska.

clue.text: Old author a model set up

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means written upwards, so the model word reverses

parts.note: to pose is to model, as for a painter

explanation.surface: An ancient writer used a model he had arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek teller of fables.

clue.text: Ran estate in eccentric way breeding aardvarks, say

indicators.note: running something in an eccentric way means oddly, signalling the letters of ran and estate are jumbled

explanation.surface: A farmer managed his land oddly by raising aardvarks.
explanation.definitionFit: Aardvarks are an example of creatures that eat ants and termites, so 'say' marks an example.

clue.text: One who judges animals, tailless kind

parts.note: asses are donkeys, animals

indicators.note: tailless means the kind word loses its last letter

parts.note: a sort is a kind or type

explanation.surface: Someone judges animals, specifically a breed lacking tails.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessor evaluates or judges things, such as property values or competition entries.

clue.text: Put a stop to hoax? Endless nonsense

indicators.note: Endless means the hoax word loses its final letter

parts.note: to kid is to hoax or trick
bosh is informal British for nonsense

explanation.surface: Someone wants to end a prank, calling it endless rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: To kibosh something, or put the kibosh on it, is to stop or crush it.

clue.text: Wall hanging records trial

parts.note: tapes are recordings
a try is an attempt or trial

explanation.surface: An embroidered wall decoration documents a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapestry is a woven fabric picture traditionally hung on walls.

clue.text: Free Turkish commander back in Moroccan port

indicators.note: back tells us the words for free and Turkish commander are read in reverse together

parts.note: to rid is to free
an aga was an Ottoman military commander

explanation.surface: A Turkish officer is released and returns to a North African harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the whole run RIDAGA, not just one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Agadir is a city and seaport on Morocco's Atlantic coast.
